primitives.name: Team Skill Aggregation
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Verdict:** ADAPT — the MAX-vs-SUM aggregation question is worth porting to GSE's unit/team rating construction, but the domain is esports with tiny samples, so port the method, not the results.
primitives.assumptions: Players contribute independently to team skill; aggregation methods define team strength via linear combination of member ratings.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When sample sizes are small or player skill distributions are highly skewed.

primitives.name: Elo Team Rating Update
primitives.verbatim_quote: Team rating updated μ′ = μ + K(R′ - Pr); player rating updated proportionally to contribution weight w_pj (ratio of player's rating to team rating sum).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'μ_i': 'team skill rating (dimensionless)', 'K': 'learning rate (dimensionless)', "R'_i": 'normalized observed rank (dimensionless)', 'Pr(i\\text{ wins})': 'probability of team i winning (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Win probability is modeled via logistic function over pairwise differences in team ratings.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When team compositions change frequently or when there are insufficient matches to stabilize ratings.

layer2.mapping: The Elo update rule serves as a kernel for iterative refinement of team strength estimates in GSE's state-transition system.
layer2.telemetry: Mean squared error between predicted and actual match outcomes.

This leads to distinct rank-prediction models within Elo, Glicko, and TrueSkill frameworks. In GSI, these are formalized as probabilistic mappings from player-level ratings to team-level win probabilities. The failure mode occurs when sample sizes are too small to support stable estimation of either individual or team ratings. For GSE, this translates into a layered state-space model where each aggregation type corresponds to a different belief structure over team strength. The key duality lies in whether team performance is additive (SUM), dominated by top performer (MAX), or constrained by weakest link (MIN). Each introduces a unique risk profile in forecasting outcomes.
